title: Setup-script exit 2 ('[x]abort', documented as stop the run) is treated as an ordinary failure: both installers continue with the next step and scripts/aitools reports 'Completed with errors'
observation: interactive-menus.md 'JSON field-level review' says only `abort` is global (stops the run); aitools-lib.sh prompt_diff_review header: 'Exits with code 2 on abort'. aitools-install.sh validate_and_run and aitools-install.ps1 Invoke-ValidatedScript handle any non-zero as a failed script and run the next step; scripts/aitools maps any installer non-zero (installer_rc) to 'Completed with errors'.
expected: .claude/rules/interactive-menus.md 'JSON field-level review' (abort is global, stops the run); reference/managed-file-deployment.md abort semantics.
impact: A user who chooses [x]abort in a managed-file or JSON field review still gets every later installer step run against their machine, and the run is reported as an error rather than an abort.
discoveryContext: Found by mission S5-Tools (I-02, I-24; reviewer S5-Tools-A D-07) (session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-20/21) and consolidated by S4-Review, which de-duplicated it against incidents #1-#86 (origin/main 26c37b2 registries/incidents.json). Audited: interactive-menus.md, aitools-lib.sh prompt_diff_review, aitools-install.sh validate_and_run, aitools-install.ps1 Invoke-ValidatedScript, scripts/aitools installer_rc handling.
suggestedResolution: Installer contract (reference/tool-support-decision-tree.md draft 7.5): exit 2 = user abort; runners write no failure row, stop remaining steps, render the summary, exit 2; entry points propagate 2 and print 'aborted by user'. Bash and PS1 together.

title: setup-datadog.sh deletes (rm -f) any non-Homebrew pup binary after a Homebrew install, including binaries of unknown origin
observation: setup-datadog.sh block 'Installed via go install or another method -- migrate' removes any pup that does not resolve under Homebrew with rm -f after brew install, without classifying its source or asking.
expected: Commander decision D3 / D-TS3 (session 360aa8f3-8): unknown-source installs are never auto-removed; plans/linux-install-hardening.md F1 (install first, clean up second).
impact: A user's self-built or vendor-provided pup is silently deleted on any aitools install run.
discoveryContext: Found by mission S5-Tools (I-03) (session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-20/21) and consolidated by S4-Review, which de-duplicated it against incidents #1-#86 (origin/main 26c37b2 registries/incidents.json). Audited: setup-datadog.sh (both migrate blocks), registry datadog-pup install methods.
suggestedResolution: Migrate setup-datadog to the tool support decision tree (unknown = HOLD/menu, never removed). Interim: delete the rm -f branch and report WARN + ACTION.

title: Tool setup scripts ignore AITOOLS_DRY_RUN, so 'aitools install --dry-run' installs, upgrades and removes tools (setup-go.sh can run sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go)
observation: aitools-install.sh exports AITOOLS_DRY_RUN=1 for --dry-run ('if $DRY_RUN; then export AITOOLS_DRY_RUN=1'); no tool setup script except setup-google-chrome references DRY_RUN (verified for setup-go.sh, which contains `sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go`).
expected: A dry run changes nothing (installer --dry-run contract; incident #7 lists the variable as an installer-to-child contract).
impact: A dry run, used precisely to preview, mutates the machine: installs, upgrades, and in setup-go.sh deletes a Go tree with sudo.
discoveryContext: Found by mission S5-Tools (I-22, found by S5-Tools-A, verified for setup-go.sh) (session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-20/21) and consolidated by S4-Review, which de-duplicated it against incidents #1-#86 (origin/main 26c37b2 registries/incidents.json). Audited: aitools-install.sh dry-run export, every scripts/setup-*.sh/.ps1 tool script (grep DRY_RUN).
suggestedResolution: Short term: guard acting commands in each tool script on AITOOLS_DRY_RUN (log '[DRY RUN] would ...'). Structural: the decision tree's dry-run overlay in tool_support_run. Related #7 (variable undocumented).

title: Tool registry install-method data cannot drive automation: nonPreferredMethods[].detection holds prose or install commands, and lifecycle.platformStatus holds non-enum values
observation: pandoc nonPreferredMethods detection: 'pip install pandoc', '/usr/local/bin/pandoc not from Homebrew'; go detection values all null; datadog-pup lifecycle.platformStatus.windows = 'supported (source build)'; google-chrome platformStatus macos/windows = null.
expected: reference/tool-evaluation-criteria.md 'Tool Platform States' enum; commander decision D1 (registry decides the method) requires machine-readable detection.
impact: No script can classify an existing install from registry data; status checks must special-case free text, so the registry cannot be the single source the decision tree needs.
discoveryContext: Found by mission S5-Tools (I-07, I-08) (session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-20/21) and consolidated by S4-Review, which de-duplicated it against incidents #1-#86 (origin/main 26c37b2 registries/incidents.json). Audited: registries/tool-registry.json pandoc, go, datadog-pup, google-chrome entries; tool-evaluation-criteria.md.
suggestedResolution: Schema 1.1 (draft): typed detection probes per method, nonPreferredMethods folded into install[] with preferred:false, platformStatus enum enforced by check-pre-commit 'Tool support conformance' check 5.
